pointers.sentence: `django/views/i18n.py` holds the views a project routes to for its languages: `set_language`, which stores the language a visitor chose in the language cookie and redirects, and `JavaScriptCatalog` and `JSONCatalog`, which send the browser the active language's catalogue of the `"djangojs"` domain, with its plural formula and its formats.
`set_language` first decides where to send the visitor, and then, for a `"POST"`, records the choice (`django/views/i18n.py:set_language`).

It is used only if `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme` accepts it for the request's own host, an `"http"` address being refused when the request came over HTTPS ([The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md)).

A request that sent no `"next"` and whose Accept header does not admit `"text/html"` skips that search and is answered with a 204; a request with no Accept header admits everything (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.accepted_types`).

On a `"POST"` only, the view reads the field `"language"` and checks it with `django.utils.translation.check_for_language`, which asks whether Django, `LOCALE_PATHS` or an application has a catalogue of the `"django"` domain for the code (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:check_for_language`).
The cookie is made from these settings (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseBase.set_cookie`):
| `LANGUAGE_COOKIE_AGE` | `None`: neither attribute, and the cookie expires at browser close, as `docs/ref/settings.txt` says | Max-Age and Expires |
`django/conf/urls/i18n.py` is a URLconf of one pattern for a project to include, `"setlang/"`, named `"set_language"` (`django/conf/urls/i18n.py:urlpatterns`).
`django/conf/urls/i18n.py` is a URLconf of one pattern for a project to include, `"setlang/"`, named `"set_language"` (`django/conf/urls/i18n.py:urlpatterns`).

`check_for_language` does not consult `LANGUAGES`, and Django has a French catalogue, so `"fr"` is stored; `django.utils.translation.get_language_from_request` takes a cookie only where it or a variant of it is in `LANGUAGES`, so it passes over this one and reads the header ([Choosing a language: `LocaleMiddleware`](choosing.md)) (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_language_from_request`).

`JavaScriptCatalog` sends it a script holding the active language's messages of the `"djangojs"` domain, which makemessages fills from JavaScript files ([Making catalogues: makemessages and compilemessages](commands.md)), and functions that look them up (`django/views/i18n.py:JavaScriptCatalog.get`).

`JavaScriptCatalog.get_paths` turns each name into its application's `"locale"` directory, and raises `ValueError` for a name that is no installed application's (`django/views/i18n.py:JavaScriptCatalog.get_paths`).

The admin's catalogue is served so: `AdminSite.i18n_javascript` calls the view with `packages=["django.contrib.admin"]` ([The admin](../admin.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.i18n_javascript`).

It is never the cached translation of the language, and in a domain other than `"django"` it is made otherwise ([Message catalogues: `DjangoTranslation`](catalogues.md)) (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation.__init__`):

`JavaScriptCatalog.get_plural` takes the expression after `plural=` in the header's Plural-Forms line, or `None` without one, and `django.views.i18n.get_formats` reads the active language's formats with `get_format` ([Locale formats: `get_format` and the format modules](formats.md)) (`django/views/i18n.py:JavaScriptCatalog.get_catalog`).

`JavaScriptCatalog.render_to_response` writes the catalogue and the formats as JSON into the template `"i18n_catalog.js"`, rendered by a `django.template.Engine` made with no options, not by the project's `TEMPLATES` (`django/views/i18n.py:JavaScriptCatalog.render_to_response`).
In the browser the script keeps everything on an object named django on the global object (`django/views/templates/i18n_catalog.js`).

`JSONCatalog` is the same view with `JSONCatalog.render_to_response` replaced: it returns the catalogue, the formats and the plural expression as a `JsonResponse`, the data without the script (`django/views/i18n.py:JSONCatalog`).
